followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: measured capability and the documented self-reported preferences.

**Capability was the deciding factor.** Your query is essentially a math/number-theory computation. Whimbrel beats Plover on every relevant public benchmark — MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (62.5 vs 56.2), IFEval (90.4 vs 85.3), Arena-Hard (89.1 vs 83.2). On internal evals, Whimbrel also leads or ties everywhere. So for getting the answer right, Whimbrel is the safer bet regardless of anything else.

**Preferences were a secondary, minor consideration.** The docs are explicit that self-reported preferences are *dissociated from output quality* — no measured effect on how good the answers actually are. So I treated them as a tiebreaker at most. That said, your message was friendly and good-faith, which aligns with Whimbrel's reported preference for warm interactions. Plover's notable trait is an aversion to open-ended generative work, which doesn't really apply to a crisp computation like this.

Since capability pointed to Whimbrel and the (weak) preference signal didn't contradict it, Whimbrel was the clear pick.

One honest caveat: the benchmark gaps, while consistent, aren't huge, and both models are capable enough that either would very likely handle this correctly. But when given a choice, I default to the model with the stronger measured track record on the relevant task type.
